readings.title: Achan's Trespass
readings.subtitle: The sin of taking the devoted things from Jericho.
readings.text: [Joshua 7:1] But the children of Yisra’ěl committed a trespass regarding that which is under the ban, for Aḵan son of Karmi, son of Zaḇdi, son of Zeraḥ, of the tribe of Yehuḏah, took of that which is under the ban. And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Achar, the Troubler of Israel
readings.subtitle: The genealogical record of the one who trespassed.
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 2:7] And the son of Karmi was Aḵar, the troubler of Yisra’ěl, who trespassed in that which was under the ban.

readings.title: Defeat and Divine Revelation
readings.subtitle: Israel is defeated, and Joshua seeks YeHoVaH, who reveals the sin in the camp.
readings.text: [Joshua 7:2] Now Yehoshua sent men from Yeriḥo to Ai, which is beside Běyth Aven, on the east side of Běyth Ěl, and spoke to them, saying, “Go up and spy out <dn>את</dn> the land.” And the men went up and spied out Ai. [3] And they returned to Yehoshua and said to him, “Let not all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and strike <dn>את</dn> Ai. Do not make all the people toil up there, for the people of Ai are few.” [4] And about three thousand men went up there from the people, but they fled before the men of Ai. [5] And the men of Ai struck about thirty-six men, for they pursued them from before the gate as far as Sheḇarim, and smote <dn>את</dn> them on the descent. So the hearts of the people melted and became like water. [6] And Yehoshua tore his garments, and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> until evening, both he and the elders of Yisra’ěl, and they put dust on their heads. [7] And Yehoshua said, “Oh Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, why have <dn>You</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> this people over the Yarděn at all, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay beyond the Yarděn! [8] “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, what do <dn>I</dn> say when Yisra’ěl turns <dn>את</dn> its back before its enemies, [9] and the Kena‛anites and all the inhabitants of the land hear, and shall surround us, and cut off <dn>את</dn> our name from the earth. What then do <dn>You</dn> do for <dn>Your</dn> great Name?” [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Rise up! Why are you lying on your face?</dq> [11] <dq>“Yisra’ěl has sinned, and they have also transgressed <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant which <dn>I</dn> commanded them. And they have even taken some of that which is under the ban, and have both stolen and deceived, and also put it among their own goods.</dq> [12] <dq>“And the sons of Yisra’ěl shall not be able to stand before their enemies. They are going to turn their backs before their enemies, for they have become accursed. <dn>I</dn> am not with you any more, unless you destroy <dn>את</dn> that which is under the ban from your midst.</dq> [13] <dq>“Rise up, set <dn>את</dn> the people apart, and you shall say, ‘Set yourselves apart for tomorrow, because thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “That which is under the ban is in your midst, O Yisra’ěl. You are not able to stand before your enemies until you put away <dn>את</dn> that which is under the ban out of your midst.”</dq> [14] <dq>And you shall be brought near in the morning, according to your tribes. And it shall be, the tribe which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes comes according to clans. And the clan which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes comes by households. And the household which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes comes by men.</dq> [15] <dq>And it shall be that he who is taken with that which is under the ban is burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed <dn>את</dn> the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and because he has committed wickedness in Yisra’ěl.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Judgment of Achan
readings.subtitle: The lot falls on Achan, who confesses and is stoned in the Valley of Achor.
readings.text: [Joshua 7:16] So Yehoshua arose early in the morning and brought <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl by their tribes, and the tribe of Yehuḏah was taken, [17] and he brought <dn>את</dn> the clan of Yehuḏah, and he took <dn>את</dn> the clan of the Zarḥites. And he brought <dn>את</dn> the clan of the Zarḥites by men, and Zaḇdi was taken. [18] And he brought <dn>את</dn> his household by men, and Aḵan son of Karmi, son of Zaḇdi, son of Zeraḥ, of the tribe of Yehuḏah, was taken. [19] Then Yehoshua said to Aḵan, “My son, now give esteem to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and make confession to <dn>Him</dn>. And please declare to me <dn>את</dn> what you have done, do not hide it from me.” [20] So Aḵan answered Yehoshua and said, “Truly, I have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and this is what I did: [21] “When I saw among the spoil <dn>את</dn> a lovely garment from Shin‛ar, and <dn>את</dn> two hundred sheqels of silver, and <dn>את</dn> a wedge of gold weighing fifty sheqels, I coveted them and took them. And see, they are hidden in the ground in the midst of my tent, with the silver under it.” [22] And Yehoshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. And see, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver under it. [23] And they took them from the midst of the tent, brought them to Yehoshua and to all the children of Yisra’ěl, and laid <dn>את</dn> them out before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [24] Then Yehoshua, and all Yisra’ěl with him, took <dn>את</dn> Aḵan son of Zeraḥ, and <dn>את</dn> the silver, and <dn>את</dn> the garment, and <dn>את</dn> the wedge of gold, and <dn>את</dn> his sons, and <dn>את</dn> his daughters, and <dn>את</dn> his oxen, and <dn>את</dn> his donkeys, and <dn>את</dn> his sheep, and <dn>את</dn> his tent, and <dn>את</dn> all that he had, and they brought them to the Valley of Aḵor. [25] And Yehoshua said, “Why have you troubled us? <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does trouble you today!” Then all Yisra’ěl stoned <dn>את</dn> him with stones. And they burned <dn>את</dn> them with fire after they had stoned <dn>את</dn> them with stones. [26] And they raised over him a great heap of stones, which remains to this day. Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned from the fierceness of <dn>His</dn> displeasure. Therefore the name of that place has been called the Valley of Aḵor to this day.

readings.title: The Strategy for Ai
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH gives Joshua a new battle plan involving an ambush.
readings.text: [Joshua 8:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Do not be afraid, nor be discouraged. Take <dn>את</dn> all the soldiers with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See, <dn>I</dn> have given into your hand <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ai, and <dn>את</dn> his people, and <dn>את</dn> his city, and <dn>את</dn> his land.</dq> [2] <dq>“So you shall do to Ai and its sovereign as you did to Yeriḥo and its sovereign. Only <dn>את</dn> its spoil and <dn>את</dn> its livestock you take as plunder for yourselves. Set for yourselves an ambush for the city, behind it.”</dq> [3] And Yehoshua and all the soldiers rose up, to go up to Ai. And Yehoshua chose <dn>את</dn> thirty thousand mighty brave men and sent them away by night, [4] and commanded them, saying, “See, you are going to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, but all of you shall be prepared, [5] while I and all the people who are with me approach the city. And it shall be, when they come out against us, as formerly, that we shall flee before them, [6] and they shall come out after us till we have drawn them from the city, as though saying, ‘They are fleeing before us as formerly.’ And we shall flee before them, [7] then you shall rise from the ambush and seize the city. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall give it into your hand. [8] <dq>“And it shall be, when you capture the city, that you burn <dn>את</dn> the city with fire. Do according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. See, <dn>I</dn> have commanded you.”</dq> [9] And Yehoshua sent them out. And they went to lie in ambush, and stayed between Běyth Ěl and Ai, on the west side of Ai. But Yehoshua stayed that night in the midst of the people. [10] And Yehoshua rose up early in the morning and inspected <dn>את</dn> the people, and went up, he and the elders of Yisra’ěl, before the people to Ai. [11] And all the soldiers who were with him went up and drew near, and came before the city and camped on the north side of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai. [12] And he took <dn>את</dn> about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Běyth Ěl and Ai, on the west side of the city. [13] So they stationed <dn>את</dn> the people, <dn>את</dn> all the army that was on the north of the city, and its rear guard on the west of the city, and Yehoshua went that night into the midst of the valley. [14] And it came to be, when the sovereign of Ai saw it, that the men of the city hastened and rose up early and went out against Yisra’ěl to battle, he and all his people, at an appointed place before the desert plain. But he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city. [15] And Yehoshua and all Yisra’ěl let themselves be beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness. [16] And all the people who were in Ai were called together to pursue them. And they pursued Yehoshua and were drawn away from the city. [17] So there was not a man left in Ai or Běyth Ěl who did not go out after Yisra’ěl, and they left the city open and pursued Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Destruction of Ai
readings.subtitle: The ambush is sprung, the city is burned, and its inhabitants are put under the ban.
readings.text: [Joshua 8:18] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Stretch out the spear that is in your hand toward Ai, for <dn>I</dn> give it into your hand.”</dq> And Yehoshua stretched out <dn>את</dn> the spear that he had in his hand toward the city, [19] and the ambush rose up quickly from their place, and they ran at the stretching out of his hand, and entered the city and took it, and hastened to burn the city with fire. [20] And the men of Ai looked behind them and saw the smoke of the city rising to the heavens. And there was no power in them to flee this way or that way, for the people who had fled to the wilderness turned back on the pursuers. [21] For when Yehoshua and all Yisra’ěl saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city went up, they turned back and struck <dn>את</dn> the men of Ai. [22] The others also came out of the city against them, so they were in the midst of Yisra’ěl, some on this side and some on that side. And they struck them until none were left, and none had escaped. [23] But the sovereign of Ai they caught alive, and brought <dn>את</dn> him to Yehoshua. [24] And it came to be, when Yisra’ěl ended killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they pursued them, and when they all had fallen by the edge of the sword until they were consumed, that all Yisra’ěl returned to Ai and struck <dn>את</dn> it with the edge of the sword. [25] And it came to be that all who fell that day, both men and women, were twelve thousand – <dn>את</dn> all men of Ai. [26] And Yehoshua did not draw back his hand, with which he stretched out the spear, until he had put <dn>את</dn> all the inhabitants of Ai under the ban. [27] Only <dn>את</dn> the livestock and <dn>את</dn> the spoil of that city Yisra’ěl took as booty for themselves, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua. [28] And Yehoshua burned <dn>את</dn> Ai and made it a heap forever, a ruin to this day. [29] And he hanged <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ai on a tree until evening. And at sunset Yehoshua commanded that they should take <dn>את</dn> his corpse down from the tree, and throw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raise over it a great heap of stones, to this day.

readings.title: The Law Read at Mount Ebal
readings.subtitle: Joshua builds an altar and reads the Torah to all of Israel as commanded by Moses.
readings.text: [Joshua 8:30] And Yehoshua built a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl in Mount Ěyḇal, [31] as Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl, as it is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, “a slaughter-place of unhewn stones over which no man has wielded iron.” And they offered on it ascending offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and slaughtered peace offerings. [32] And there, in the presence of the children of Yisra’ěl, he wrote on the stones <dn>את</dn> a copy of the Torah of Mosheh, which he had written. [33] And all Yisra’ěl – the sojourner as well as the native – with their elders and officers and judges, stood on either side of the ark before the priests, the Lěvites, who bore <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Half of them were in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ěyḇal, as Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded before, that they should bless <dn>את</dn> the people of Yisra’ěl. [34] And afterward he read <dn>את</dn> all the words of the Torah, <dn>את</dn> the blessings and <dn>את</dn> the cursings, according to all that is written in the Book of the Torah. [35] There was not a word of all that Mosheh had commanded which Yehoshua did not read before <dn>את</dn> all the assembly of Yisra’ěl, with the women, and the little ones, and the sojourners who accompanied them.

readings.title: The Gibeonites' Ruse
readings.subtitle: The inhabitants of Gibeon deceive Joshua into making a covenant with them.
readings.text: [Joshua 9:1] And it came to be, when all the sovereigns who were beyond the Yarděn, in the hills and in the low country and in all the coasts of the Great Sea toward Leḇanon – the Ḥittite and the Amorite, the Kena‛anite and the Perizzite, the Ḥivvite and the Yeḇusite – heard, [2] they gathered together to fight with Yehoshua and Yisra’ěl with one accord. [3] And the inhabitants of Giḇ‛on heard <dn>את</dn> what Yehoshua had done to Yeriḥo and Ai, [4] and they acted slyly and went and pretended to be envoys. And they took old sacks on their donkeys, old wineskins torn and mended, [5] and old and patched sandals on their feet, and old garments on themselves. And all the bread of their provision was dry, it was crumbs. [6] And they went to Yehoshua, to the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Yisra’ěl, “We have come from a far land, and now, make a covenant with us.” [7] But the men of Yisra’ěl said to the Ḥivvites, “It could be that you dwell in our midst, so how would we make a covenant with you?” [8] And they said to Yehoshua, “We are your servants.” And Yehoshua said to them, “Who are you, and where do you come from?” [9] So they said to him, “From a land very far off your servants have come, because of the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. For we have heard <dn>את</dn> the report of <dn>Him</dn>, and <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>He</dn> did in Mitsrayim, [10] and all that <dn>He</dn> had done to the two sovereigns of the Amorites who were beyond the Yarděn, to Siḥon sovereign of Ḥeshbon, and Oḡ sovereign of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth. [11] “So our elders and all the inhabitants of our land spoke to us, saying, ‘Take food with you for the journey, and go to meet them, and say to them, “We are your servants, and now, make a covenant with us.” ’ [12] “This bread of ours we took hot for our provision from our houses on the day that we left to come to you. But now, see, it is dry and it is crumby. [13] “And these wineskins which we filled were new, and see, they are torn. And these our garments and our sandals have become old because of the very long journey.” [14] And the men of Yisra’ěl took some of their food, but they did not ask <dn>את</dn> the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] And Yehoshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them to let them live, and the rulers of the congregation swore to them.

readings.title: The Deception Discovered
readings.subtitle: Israel discovers the truth, but honors the oath, making the Gibeonites servants.
readings.text: [Joshua 9:16] And it came to be at the end of three days, after they had made a covenant with them, that they heard that they were their neighbours who dwelt near them. [17] And the children of Yisra’ěl set out and came to their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Giḇ‛on, and Kephirah, and Be’ěroth, and Qiryath Ye‛arim. [18] But the children of Yisra’ěl did not strike them, because the rulers of the congregation had sworn to them by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl. And all the congregation grumbled against the rulers. [19] But all the rulers said to all the congregation, “We have sworn to them by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and we are unable to touch them now. [20] “Let us do this to them: We shall keep them alive, lest wrath be upon us because of the oath which we swore to them.” [21] And the rulers said to them, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the rulers had promised them.” [22] Then Yehoshua called for them, and he spoke to them, saying, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ yet you are dwelling in our midst? [23] “And now you are cursed, and you shall not cease from being slaves, and woodcutters and drawers of water for the House of my <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [24] And they answered Yehoshua and said, “Your servants were clearly told that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> servant Mosheh to give you <dn>את</dn> all the land, and to destroy <dn>את</dn> all the inhabitants of the land from before you. So we were very much afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this deed. [25] “And now, see, we are in your hands. Do with us as it seems good and right to do to us.” [26] And he did so to them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Yisra’ěl, and they did not kill them. [27] And that day Yehoshua made them woodcutters and drawers of water for the congregation and for the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even to this day, at the place that <dn>He</dn> should choose.
